inputs.share_count_basis: Q2-2026 diluted weighted average (192.8M, 10-Q / ex-99.1 2026-08-05). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the ~$1B FY2026 buyback is the cash mechanism keeping the count flat (charging both would double-count).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back $90.2M (Q4-25 ex-99.1, XBRL ShareBasedCompensation). Equity-award tax withholding is not separately tagged (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation empty); financing shows net proceeds of $39.7M from employee plans, so withholding is small and netted. reported_fcf is the COMPANY definition (OCF 1,697.1 - instruments 300.5 - other PP&E 224.5 = 1,172.1); the Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow (1,472.6) omits instrument additions and overstates FCF by ~$300M/yr.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: 10y UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 -> cost of equity ~8.8%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.0% (BBB, ~5% pre-tax); market-value weights ~70/30 equity/debt -> ~7.4% computed. Base uses 8.0% (rounded up for a large-cap with a decade of organic growth below the ortho market). Same WACC in every scenario: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$233M liability FY2025, ~$68M/yr cash cost): lease expense sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA, so lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is immaterial (~$1M/quarter of earnings); ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 1/2: US operating company, medtech/orthopaedics; no bank/REIT/holdco features, no live corporate action). Fresh build - no prior DCF or memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 revenue $8,231.5M; FY2026 growth set inside the August-2026 raised guidance (reported +3.9% to +4.9%; organic cc +2.25% to +3.25%; Paragon 28 adds ~110bps through April 2026). EBITDA margin is GAAP EBITDA + SBC (pre-SBC, after recurring special items): FY23 31.5%, FY24 31.0%, FY25 27.7% (Paragon 28/Monogram deal and integration costs, restructuring), H1-26 30.2%. Special items have recurred every year at ZBH, so the path is anchored to GAAP not 'adjusted'. D&A ~13% of revenue includes ~$666M/yr of acquired-intangible amortization (largely Biomet, much of it not tax-deductible) - the cash tax rate on EBIT (~32%) is therefore above the ~17-18% adjusted book rate: FY25 cash taxes $376.9M plus the ~$60M tax shield on $293M net interest, over unlevered EBIT ~$1.1B. Capex = PP&E + surgical instrument additions + acquired intangibles (FY25 224.5+300.5+52.4 = 7.0% of revenue). Working capital is a consumer of cash (inventories $2.27B + receivables $1.77B vs payables): wc_capture -35% of the revenue increase. Buybacks: $487M FY25, $500.8M H1-26, guided up to $1B for FY26 - the flat share count is being funded. Dividend $0.96/yr (~$190M). Metrics.csv FreeCashFlow excludes instrument additions; owner FCF here uses the company's own FCF definition.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic revenue growth (FY2026 organic cc guidance 2.25-3.25%, FY25 organic cc 3.9%) plus modest M&A/pricing; reported revenue CAGRs include Paragon 28 (Apr-25) and a COVID-depressed FY2020 base
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.8-1.8%) diverges >30% from revenue (~6%) and EPS CAGRs: book value is held down by buybacks and dividends and was inflated by the 2015 Biomet stock deal; EPS CAGR (47.9% 3yr) runs off a depressed FY2022 GAAP base ($1.10) and FY2020 was a loss, so neither is usable. Revenue/organic growth selected.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGR is on the CSV basis (OCF - PP&E - SBC, which omits instrument additions): FY2020 1,018.8 -> FY2025 1,382.4 = 6.3%/yr. FY2022 OCF is missing from the CSV so the 3-year FCF CAGR is null. SBC (~1.1-1.4% of revenue) is small and stable, so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow.

base.narrative: Organic growth 3-4% plus ~0.5-1pp from tuck-ins/pricing; margins recover from the FY25 deal-cost trough toward FY23-24 levels as Paragon 28 integration and the US go-to-market rebuild finish.

scenario_narratives.base: Zimmer Biomet stays the #1 hip/knee implant franchise growing roughly with a 4-5% procedure market but still losing a little knee share: organic growth of 3-4% (knees ~1-2%, hips ~4-5%, S.E.T. 4-6% as Paragon 28 foot & ankle compounds, Technology & Data double-digit from ROSA and Monogram), reported growth 4-4.5%. FY2025's deal and restructuring costs fade and GAAP EBITDA margin (pre-SBC) recovers from 27.7% to ~31.5%, still below the 33%+ peers earn. Cash conversion stays held back by ~7% of revenue in instrument sets and PP&E and an inventory-heavy working-capital model. Buybacks of ~$1B/yr keep the count flat.
scenario_narratives.bull: The innovation cycle finally lands: ROSA (knee, hip, and the new shoulder system) plus Monogram's semi-autonomous robot narrow the gap to Stryker's Mako installed base, the Persona/Oxford cementless knee portfolio stops the US share bleed, and the specialised US sales-force rebuild under the new Americas leadership lifts productivity. Organic growth reaches 5-6% for several years as S.E.T. (sports, extremities, Paragon 28 foot & ankle) and the ASC shift add mix, and EBITDA margin expands to ~33.5% on operating leverage and the end of serial restructuring.
scenario_narratives.bear: Mako-driven share loss in knees continues (ZBH knees grew 0.4% in Q2-26 against a mid-single-digit market), the US go-to-market reorganisation and repeated leadership turnover disrupt the sales channel, and China volume-based procurement plus European pricing compress international price. Organic growth settles at ~2.5%, special items keep recurring so margins drift to ~29%, and instrument capex rises to defend robotics placements. Exit multiple compresses to 13x as ZBH is valued as an ex-growth share donor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default because ZBH has under-delivered its organic growth ambitions for a decade (knee share loss to Stryker Mako, serial restructuring, leadership churn including the Sept-2026 Americas reorganisation). Base 50% matches the raised and reiterated FY2026 guidance. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (robotics catch-up, knee share stabilisation, sales-force productivity, margin expansion).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mature, cash-generative orthopaedic franchise with a durable installed base of surgeons and instrument sets, valued on owner FCF (company FCF definition, including instrument additions, less SBC) with an unlevered component build and 10-year horizon while margins recover from the FY2025 trough. The Metrics.csv FCF excludes ~$300M/yr of instrument additions and must not be used as the base.
key_risks_to_valuation: Knee share loss to Stryker Mako continuing (knees +0.4% in Q2-26)
US go-to-market rebuild and senior leadership turnover disrupting sales execution
Recurring 'special items' (restructuring, integration, quality remediation, EU MDR) - margin recovery assumes they fade
Pricing: China VBP, European tenders, US hospital/ASC pricing pressure
Leverage ~2.9x net debt / EBITDA after Paragon 28 and Monogram; $1.2B current maturities in the next 12 months
Terminal value carries most of the value; terminal cap multiple binds
